summary: The low-body guide reduced the round shell-like torso introduced by the first combined plate/thagomizer candidate. The best result used the previous angular-plate candidate as a low-weight IP-Adapter source and the new low-body guide as ControlNet. Using the previous round-body candidate or tail-room candidate as style references reintroduced shell-like torsos or weakened the thagomizer.
primaryRejectReasons: round-body style reference preserves the shell-like torso failure
tail-room reference naturalizes the scene but keeps a rounded body and small tail spikes
selected candidate still needs close review because tail spikes are small and some legs are hidden
plate separation is improved at atlas scale but still not final-approved
usefulFindings: A lower, longer body control target is more useful than simply increasing ControlNet strength on the first combined reference.
The angular-plate style source preserved a cleaner Stegosaurus body than the previous plate/thagomizer candidate.
Future Stegosaurus passes should avoid using shell-like candidates as style references unless the body is masked or repaired first.
nextRoute: Keep the low-body candidate first for MVP comparison. For approval, refine the tail-spike count and plate separation without reintroducing shell-like torso drift, or train a focused stegosaurian LoRA from reviewed synthetic seeds.
